 Dated : 8th January, 2025
ORDER This is an application filed on behalf of the appellants under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, praying for condoning a delay of 3527 days in filing the appeal.
The appellants are the petitioners in OP(MV).858/2004 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alappuzha.

They are the wife,
children and parents of deceased Ankajan who died on account of the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.5.2004.

The Tribunal passed the impugned award on 31.1.2011,
by which a compensation of Rs.3,98,106/- was allowed.
The present appeal has been preferred against the said award, after a huge delay of 3527 days.

2. The 1st appellant who filed the affidavit supporting the petition, would swear that on the sudden demise of her husband, the entire burden of the family consisting of minor daughters fell upon her shoulder.
She started the work of carrying fish and selling the same door to door and using the meagre income derived from the same, she was looking after her family.
Being a layman, she was not aware of her legal right of filing appeal against the award.
Her counsel before the Tribunal did not inform her about such a right.

In the year 2018, during the course of fish selling, accidentally she met her present counsel and on hearing about the death of her husband in an accident, her counsel enlightened her about the right.

Thereafter, she applied for a certified copy of the award on 13.8.2018 and she received a copy of the C.M.Appln.1/2020 in M.A.C.A.2912/2020 award on 11.5.2018 from the counsel at Alappuzha and handed over the same to the present counsel on 13.5.2018.

Further, according to the 1 st appellant, her present counsel shifted her office from Kadavanthra to Thrikkakkara and during the shifting of the office, the case bundle got misplaced and it was traced out only on 12.10.2020.
Thereafter, the counsel prepared the appeal and filed the same.
According to her, it was in the above context that there occurred a delay of 3527 days in preferring the appeal.
3. The application was strongly opposed by the 3rd respondent/insurer by filing a counter affidavit and contending mainly the following:

The reasons stated by the petitioners that the file was misplaced in the office of the counsel and it has been traced out only in 2020, cannot be believed as the award was passed on 31.1.2011 and a copy application was filed only on 13.3.2018.
The petitioners were not vigilant in conducting the case and the reason for the delay is not satisfactory.
Since there is no sufficient grounds for condoning the delay, the 3rd respondent prayed for dismissing the C.M. Application.
4. Now the point that arise for consideration is the following :

Whether the reason offered by the petitioner for the inordinate delay of 3527 days in Sarjini vs S John Pious on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188240139/
2 filing the appeal is sufficient ?

sentences.text:
5. Heard Sri.P.S.Geethakumari, the learned counsel for the petitioners and N.S.Najeeb, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
6.
The point:- The petitioners are the widow, children and parents of the C.M.Appln.1/2020 in M.A.C.A.2912/2020 deceased Ankajan, who died in a road traffic accident on 20.5.2004.
The Tribunal passed the impugned award as early as on 31.1.2011, while they have preferred the present appeal only on 14.10.2020.
The petitioners have offered two reasons for the delay in filing the appeal.
The reason for the period from 31.1.2011 to March 2018 was that she was not aware of her right of appeal and that her counsel before the Tribunal did not inform her about such a right.

For the subsequent delay the reason offered by her is that when her new counsel informed her about the right of appeal, she applied for certified copy of the Award and the copy was delivered to her counsel on 11.5.2018.
She received the certified copy of the Award from the counsel and handed over the same to her present counsel on 13.5.2018.

According to her, thereafter, there was shifting of the office of her present counsel from Kadavanthra to Thrikkakara and in that process her file was misplaced and it was traced out only on 12.10.2020.

7. The learned counsel for the respondent relied upon the decision of the learned Single Bench of this Court in Sasi.K. v. S.Asokan (MACA 2038/2021) in support of his argument that condonation of long delay would cause substantial prejudice hardships and injustice to the respondents.
In the decision in Suraja v. Prkashan 2017 (1) KLT, SN 16 (C.No.13), the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that if there is gross negligence on the part of the applicant, the delay cannot be condoned.

8. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon the decision of a Division bench of this Court in Musthafa P.S. v. Nazeera Beegum and Others, 2020 (6) KHC 474, in which this Court held that what ought to be the C.M.Appln.1/2020 in M.A.C.A.2912/2020 primary concern to the Court is not the length of delay, but the sufficiency of explanation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He has also relied upon the decision of the Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court in Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Tanushree Chakraborty, 2020 KHC 5440, wherein while condoning the delay of six years and nine months, the court observed that "naturally a party litigant ought not be made to suffer for the latches of his learned advocate, particularly when it involves the benefit under a welfare statute".
9.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Tanushree Chakraborty, 2020 KHC 5440
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As contended by the 3rd respondent, there was lack of due diligence on the part of the petitioners in approaching the court in time.
However, it is to be noted that the 1st appellant is a fish merchant who used to carry fish and sell the same from door to door.
The other appellants are her children and the parents of the deceased.
It appears that all of them are laymen coming from the lower strata of the society.
It is true that ignorance of law is not an excuse.
But, at the same time, we should not forget the ground realities in the life of a hapless widowed fisher woman who ekes out the means of her livelihood by carrying fish and selling from door to door.
Therefore, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve her claim that they were not aware of the right of appeal, till they were enlightened by their present counsel.

sentences.text: It is also to be noticed that the appeal relates to claim for compensation on account of the death of her husband who died in a road traffic accident.

As held in the decision in Tanushree Chakraborty (supra), a party litigant ought not be made to suffer for the latches of his learned advocate,
particularly when it involves the benefit under a welfare statute.

Since this application was filed by a widowed fisher woman C.M.Appln.1/2020 in M.A.C.A.2912/2020 claiming compensation on account of the death of her husband in a road traffic accident, I am inclined to condone the delay of 3527 days, but on condition that they shall waive interest for the period of delay in filing the appeal.

Sd/-
C.Pratheep Kumar, Judge Mrcs/18.12.
